prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
context: The aftershocks continued through the night and only began to ____ shortly before dawn, when the rescue teams were finally allowed into the collapsed wing.
explanation: abate 指風暴、疼痛、噪音這類「強度」逐漸減弱、緩和，可以不接受詞。句中主詞是餘震，配上 only began to … shortly before dawn，講的正是強度隨時間轉弱，而不是有人把它取消或放棄。

distractorExplanations.b: abolish 是以制度或法令「廢除」某種做法（abolish slavery、abolish a tax），需要有人為的決定，餘震不能被廢除。
distractorExplanations.c: abstain 是不及物動詞，意思是「棄權、自我克制」，須說 abstain from something，主詞必須是有意志的人。
distractorExplanations.d: abandon 是「棄置、中途放棄」某件事物，強調行為者撇下受詞離開，與強度自然轉弱無關，而且此處沒有受詞。

prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
context: Because the two laboratories are ____ to each other, vibration from the centrifuge in one is picked up by the electron microscope in the other.
explanation: adjacent 表示「相鄰的、緊鄰的」，固定用 be adjacent to something。句中兩間實驗室彼此緊鄰，離心機的振動才會傳到隔壁，是典型的空間相鄰關係。

distractorExplanations.a: adhesive 是「有黏性的」，形容膠帶或黏著劑，與空間位置無關。
distractorExplanations.c: adjunct 作形容詞時指「附屬的、兼任的」（an adjunct professor），描述隸屬關係而非位置，也不搭配 to each other 這樣的句型。
distractorExplanations.d: autonomous 是「自主運作的」，強調不受外部控制，正好與句中互相干擾的情況相反，也不接介系詞 to。

prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
context: Regulators require that any ____ reaction observed during the trial be reported within twenty-four hours, even when the investigator is convinced the drug was not responsible.
explanation: adverse 是「不利的、有害的」，adverse reaction／adverse effects 是醫藥與法規文件的固定搭配，指對受試者造成傷害的反應，正符合須在二十四小時內通報的情境。

distractorExplanations.a: averse 與 adverse 只差一個字母，但意思是「不願意的、反感的」，形容人的態度且須用 be averse to，不能修飾 reaction。
distractorExplanations.b: arduous 是「艱鉅費力的」，形容任務或旅程，反應本身無所謂費不費力。
distractorExplanations.d: ambient 指「周遭環境的」（ambient temperature、ambient noise），描述背景條件，不帶有害的意思。

prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
context: The dashboard does not keep every individual reading; it ____ them by the hour, which is the only reason a full year of sensor data fits in one table.
explanation: aggregate 作動詞是「彙總」，把分散的數值合併成總計或群組，常搭配 data、results。句中儀表板把逐筆讀數按小時併成一筆，資料量才壓得下來，正是 aggregate 的核心用法。

distractorExplanations.a: allocate 是把資源「分配」給不同用途（allocate a budget to a project），方向與把資料合併起來相反。
distractorExplanations.b: appropriate 作動詞指「撥款」或「擅自佔用」，受詞通常是經費或財物，不會是感測器讀數。
distractorExplanations.c: alleviate 是「減輕」痛苦、負擔或壓力，受詞是負面的事物，不能接資料。

prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
context: The chief engineer was ____ that the launch be postponed, and she repeated the demand at every review until the board finally gave way.
explanation: adamant 指「堅決不改變立場」，常用 be adamant that 加子句，且該子句多用原形動詞的假設語氣。句中她在每一次審查會上重複同一項要求直到董事會讓步，正是立場毫不動搖。

distractorExplanations.b: ambivalent 是對同一件事「同時抱持兩種相反感受」，語氣猶疑，與反覆堅持同一主張矛盾，也不接 that 子句。
distractorExplanations.c: apprehensive 是「感到不安、憂慮」，描述情緒而非立場，常用 apprehensive about something。
distractorExplanations.d: amenable 是「願意接受、好說話」，意思與堅持不讓正好相反，且須用 be amenable to something。

prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
context: Rather than resign in protest, the two junior partners ____ in a settlement that they privately regarded as indefensible.
explanation: acquiesce 是正式用語，指「默許」——不出聲反對地接受，但未必真心贊同，固定用 acquiesce in／to something。句中他們沒有辭職抗議，心裡卻認為和解方案站不住腳，正是這種表面順從、內心保留的態度。

distractorExplanations.a: demur 是「表示異議、面有難色」，用 demur at something，語意與默默接受相反。
distractorExplanations.c: dissent 是公開表達不同意見，用 dissent from something，與句首「沒有辭職抗議」的讓步語氣衝突。
distractorExplanations.d: intervene 是「介入干預」，指主動出手改變事態，也不是接受既成的和解結果。

prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
context: The memory spike showed up on one node every Sunday night and on no other machine; nobody could account for the ____ until an engineer checked the server's time-zone setting.
explanation: anomaly 指單一觀測值「偏離常態、因此需要解釋」的異常現象。句中只有一個節點、每逢週日出現尖峰，是明顯脫離常軌又值得追查的觀測值，account for the anomaly 也是標準搭配。

distractorExplanations.a: discrepancy 指兩份紀錄或兩個數字「對不起來」，必須有兩個可比對的來源；這裡只有單一節點的觀測值偏離常態。
distractorExplanations.b: deficiency 是「不足、缺陷」，指少了應有的東西，但記憶體用量是突然升高而非短少。
distractorExplanations.d: coincidence 是兩件事「碰巧同時發生」的巧合，句中規律地每週重現，正好說明它不是巧合。

prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
context: The ledgers, the shipping manifests and the customs stamps all ____ to the scale of the trade long before any official account of it survives.
explanation: attest to something 意思是「（證據）足以證明某事屬實」，主詞可以是人，也可以像這裡一樣是帳冊、艙單、關防等物證。句中這些紀錄共同佐證了貿易規模，正是 attest 的典型學術用法。

distractorExplanations.a: allude to 是「間接提及、暗指」，重點在說話者拐彎提到某事，而不是提供足以證實的證據。
distractorExplanations.b: adhere to 是「遵守」規則或「黏附」於表面，受詞不會是貿易規模這種待證事實。
distractorExplanations.c: ascribe 的句型是 ascribe something to something，必須先有被歸因的對象，不能只接 to。

prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
context: What the auditors found was not a subtle accounting trick but a ____ disregard for the controls: the same manager both raised the invoices and approved them.
explanation: blatant 指「明目張膽的」——不當行為做得毫不掩飾，帶有明顯的譴責語氣，blatant disregard for something 更是固定搭配。句中以 not a subtle … but a ____ 對比，明白要求一個與「隱晦」相反且負面的字。

distractorExplanations.b: benign 是「無害的、良性的」，語意正面，無法用來描述稽核人員查出的內控失守。
distractorExplanations.c: bland 是「平淡無味、乏善可陳」，形容食物或文字缺乏特色，與是否掩飾無關。
distractorExplanations.d: baffling 是「令人費解的」，但句中的問題一目了然——同一人開單又核准——並不難理解。

prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
context: In her will she ____ the entire collection to the museum, on the single condition that no item in it ever be sold.
explanation: bequeath 是遺囑用語，指「透過遺囑把財產遺贈給某人」，句型為 bequeath something to somebody。句首 In her will 已經點明是遺囑處分，收受方是博物館，正好對上這個字。

distractorExplanations.a: endow 的句型是 endow somebody／an institution with something，或 endow a chair，不能說 endow something to somebody。
distractorExplanations.c: relinquish 是「放棄」權利或職位，重點在自己撒手，不指定承接的對象，也與遺囑無關。
distractorExplanations.d: confer 是「授予」榮銜或權利，句型為 confer something on somebody，介系詞用 on 而非 to，受詞也多為學位、頭銜一類。

prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
context: Below its glass-transition temperature the polymer turns so ____ that a bracket which flexes safely at room temperature will shatter under exactly the same load.
explanation: brittle 指材料「硬而易碎」——受力時不會彎折而是直接斷裂。句中以 flexes safely 對比 shatter，說明低溫下材料失去韌性、一受力就碎，正是 brittle 的定義。

distractorExplanations.a: buoyant 是「有浮力的」，或引申為市場、情緒的「暢旺、樂觀」，與材料強度無關。
distractorExplanations.b: blunt 是「鈍的」，形容刀刃不利，或形容說話直率，與是否易碎無關。
distractorExplanations.d: bulky 是「體積龐大笨重的」，講的是尺寸而非低溫下的破壞行為。

prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
context: Every purchase above fifty dollars required three separate signatures, and new staff spent their first month learning to navigate the ____ instead of doing the work they had been hired for.
explanation: bureaucracy 指「官僚體制、繁文縟節」，強調規則與程序層層疊疊而拖垮效率，帶輕微負面評價。句中三道簽核、新人一個月都耗在應付流程上，說的正是程序本身太繁瑣。

distractorExplanations.a: hierarchy 指組織的「層級結構」，講的是誰隸屬於誰，句中抱怨的卻是手續繁複，不是職級高低。
distractorExplanations.b: autonomy 是「自主權」，意思與凡事都要簽核相反。
distractorExplanations.c: diplomacy 是「外交」或「圓融的手腕」，與內部採購流程無關。

prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
context: Because her brother had died two years before the policy was written, she was named its sole ____ and received the entire payout.
explanation: beneficiary 指保單或遺囑上「指定領受給付的人」，the sole beneficiary、name somebody as a beneficiary 都是保險與法律文件的固定說法。句中她領走全部理賠金，正是受益人。

distractorExplanations.b: benefactor 是「出錢資助他人的人」，方向相反——是給予者而不是領受者。
distractorExplanations.c: trustee 是「受託人」，替他人保管並管理財產，本身不能把款項據為己有。
distractorExplanations.d: bystander 是「旁觀者」，只是碰巧在場，與保單上的指定身分無關。

prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
context: Nobody was willing to ____ the subject of redundancies while the merger was still unannounced, so the meeting ended with the one question everyone had come to ask still unasked.
explanation: broach the subject of something 意思是「（小心翼翼地）開口提出一個敏感話題」。句中裁員話題人人迴避、終究沒人開口，正需要這個表示「首度提起」的字。

distractorExplanations.a: breach 與 broach 讀音相近但意思是「違反」合約或「突破」防線，受詞不會是 subject。
distractorExplanations.c: brandish 是「揮舞」武器或文件以示威嚇，是具體動作，不能接抽象的話題。
distractorExplanations.d: belabor 是「對已經提出的話題反覆糾纏」，前提是話題早已被提起，與這裡從頭沒人敢開口正好相反。

prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
context: After conditions inside the supplier's factories were exposed, campaigners called for a ____ of the brand until an independent inspection was allowed.
explanation: boycott 指「抵制」——集體拒買、拒用某個對象以示抗議，call for a boycott of something 是標準搭配。句中訴求是消費者停止購買該品牌直到對方接受查核，正是這個字。

distractorExplanations.a: blockade 是「封鎖」，以武力或實體手段阻斷通行與補給，屬軍事或港口用語。
distractorExplanations.b: backlash 是輿論或情緒的「強烈反彈」，是自然發生的反應，不會由人 call for，也不接 of 表達對象。
distractorExplanations.d: bailout 是政府或機構出資的「紓困」，是援救而非抗議。
